notable_absence.finding: DIRECT ANSWER TO THE ROUND'S CENTRAL QUESTION: eventing-rbac.md introduces zero new roles and zero new privileges. It reuses exactly two pre-existing axes without modification: (1) the Capella UI project-role trio Data Reader/Data Writer/Project Owner, already established for the general management plane, gating Function CRUD/deploy/undeploy/delete/export by table row; and (2) the cluster-access-credential-type Basic/Advanced axis with the single privilege round 7 could only place with no detail, privilege:capella-advanced-access-eventing-manage - which this page reveals is NEVER granted alone. Every one of the three target-keyspace rows (Source/Mutation, Metadata/Storage, Bindings) requires 'Data Read AND Eventing Manage' together, mirroring the exact bundling shape cluster-rbac.md's own Read/Write Basic-access-level table already established (a compound privilege requirement, not a single independent gate). No Eventing-specific role or privilege catalog exists anywhere in Capella.

cross_component_finding: This page's own two-heading structure ('Access Eventing with the Capella UI' / 'Access Eventing with Cluster Access Credentials') is a verbatim structural echo of cluster-rbac.md's own two-tier model (organization/project roles for the UI plane vs. cluster access credentials for the programmatic/SDK plane) - Eventing did not just reuse the same vocabulary, it reused the same page architecture for presenting that vocabulary. This is the cleanest possible negative result for the round's hypothesis: unlike Sync Gateway's channel model (which inverted the access-control direction entirely) or the Java SDK's transaction layer (which added a genuinely new concurrency primitive), Eventing's RBAC surface required no new structural layer at all - it slots into the pre-existing two-axis model perfectly, contributing only one already-known privilege name to the existing 26-member privilege:capella-advanced-access-* family.
cross_product_finding: None specific to this page - all cross-references point to Capella's own organization/project/cluster-access documentation, not to other Couchbase products.
